passages.text: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet from outside Israel.
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balaam spoke to Balak.
Balaam said, “Build seven altars for me here.”
Balaam said, “Prepare seven bulls for me here.”
Balaam said, “Prepare seven rams for me here.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בִּלְעָם֙ אֶל־ בָּלָ֔ק בְּנֵה־ לִ֥י בָזֶ֖ה שִׁבְעָ֣ה מִזְבְּחֹ֑ת וְהָכֵ֥ן לִי֙ בָּזֶ֔ה שִׁבְעָ֥ה פָרִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה אֵילִֽים׃

passages.text: So Balak did as Balaam had instructed, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balaam was a prophet.
Balaam gave instructions to Balak.
Balak obeyed Balaam’s instructions.
Balak and Balaam built altars.
They offered a bull on each altar.
They offered a ram on each altar.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ בָּלָ֔ק כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיַּ֨עַל בָּלָ֧ק וּבִלְעָ֛ם פָּ֥ר וָאַ֖יִל בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: “Stay here by your burnt offering while I am gone,” Balaam said to Balak. “Perhaps the LORD will meet with me. And whatever He reveals to me, I will tell you.” So Balaam went off to a barren height, and God met with him. “I have set up seven altars,” Balaam said, “and on each altar I have offered a bull and a ram.”
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet from Mesopotamia.
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balaam spoke to Balak.
Balaam said, “Stay here by your burnt offering.”
Balaam said, “I will go away.”
Balaam said, “Perhaps the LORD will meet with me.”
Balaam said, “Whatever the LORD shows me, I will tell you.”
Balaam left and went to a barren height.
God met with Balaam.
Balaam said to God, “I have set up seven altars.”
Balaam said, “I have offered a bull and a ram on each altar.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בִּלְעָ֜ם לְבָלָ֗ק הִתְיַצֵּב֮ עַל־ עֹלָתֶךָ֒ וְאֵֽלְכָ֗ה אוּלַ֞י יִקָּרֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לִקְרָאתִ֔י וּדְבַ֥ר מַה־ יַּרְאֵ֖נִי וְהִגַּ֣דְתִּי לָ֑ךְ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ שֶֽׁפִי׃ וַיִּקָּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אֶת־ שִׁבְעַ֤ת הַֽמִּזְבְּחֹת֙ עָרַ֔כְתִּי וָאַ֛עַל פָּ֥ר וָאַ֖יִל בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: Then the LORD put a message in Balaam’s mouth, saying, “Return to Balak and give him this message.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Balaam.
The LORD gave Balaam a message to say.
The LORD told Balaam, "Go back to Balak."
The LORD said, "Speak these words to Balak."
passages.original: וַיָּ֧שֶׂם יְהוָ֛ה דָּבָ֖ר בְּפִ֣י בִלְעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֛אמֶר שׁ֥וּב אֶל־ בָּלָ֖ק וְכֹ֥ה תְדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: So he returned to Balak, who was standing there beside his burnt offering, with all the princes of Moab.
passages.sermon: Balaam returned to Balak.\r\nBalak was standing beside his burnt offering.\r\nAll the princes of Moab stood with Balak.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣שָׁב אֵלָ֔יו וְהִנֵּ֥ה נִצָּ֖ב עַל־ עֹלָת֑וֹ ה֖וּא וְכָל־ שָׂרֵ֥י מוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: And Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Balak brought me from Aram, the king of Moab from the mountains of the east. ‘Come,’ he said, ‘put a curse on Jacob for me; come and denounce Israel!’
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
God gave Balaam a message to speak.
Balaam spoke an oracle.
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak sent for Balaam.
Balak lived in the mountains of the east, in Aram.
Balak brought Balaam from Aram.
Balak said to Balaam, “Come.”
Balak told Balaam, “Curse Jacob for me.”
Balak also said, “Come and denounce Israel.”
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר מִן־ אֲ֠רָם יַנְחֵ֨נִי בָלָ֤ק מֶֽלֶךְ־ מוֹאָב֙ מֵֽהַרְרֵי־ קֶ֔דֶם לְכָה֙ אָֽרָה־ לִּ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב וּלְכָ֖ה זֹעֲמָ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: How can I curse what God has not cursed? How can I denounce what the LORD has not denounced?
passages.sermon:
Balaam is a prophet.
Balak, king of Moab, asked Balaam to curse Israel.
God did not curse Israel.
The LORD did not denounce Israel.
Balaam said, “I cannot curse those God has not cursed.”
Balaam said, “I cannot denounce those the LORD has not denounced.”
passages.original: מָ֣ה אֶקֹּ֔ב לֹ֥א קַבֹּ֖ה אֵ֑ל וּמָ֣ה אֶזְעֹ֔ם לֹ֥א זָעַ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: For I see them from atop the rocky cliffs, and I watch them from the hills. Behold, a people dwelling apart, not reckoning themselves among the nations.
passages.sermon:
Balaam is a prophet.
Balaam speaks an oracle from God.
Balaam looks at Israel from high places.
He stands on rocky cliffs.
He watches from the hills.
He sees the people of Israel.
Israel lives apart from other nations.
Israel does not count itself among the nations.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ מֵרֹ֤אשׁ צֻרִים֙ אֶרְאֶ֔נּוּ וּמִגְּבָע֖וֹת אֲשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ הֶן־ עָם֙ לְבָדָ֣ד יִשְׁכֹּ֔ן וּבַגּוֹיִ֖ם לֹ֥א יִתְחַשָּֽׁב׃

passages.text: Who can count the dust of Jacob or number even a fourth of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous; let my end be like theirs!”
passages.sermon:
Jacob is the ancestor of the people of Israel.
Israel is a great and numerous people.
No one can count the dust of Jacob.
No one can number even a fourth of Israel.
The righteous die with honor.
Let me die the death of the righteous.
Let my end be like theirs.
passages.original: מִ֤י מָנָה֙ עֲפַ֣ר יַעֲקֹ֔ב וּמִסְפָּ֖ר אֶת־ רֹ֣בַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל תָּמֹ֤ת נַפְשִׁי֙ מ֣וֹת יְשָׁרִ֔ים וּתְהִ֥י אַחֲרִיתִ֖י כָּמֹֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Then Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies, and behold, you have only blessed them!”
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak spoke to Balaam.
Balak said, “What have you done to me?”
Balak said, “I brought you here to curse my enemies.”
Balak said, “But you have only blessed them.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בָּלָק֙ אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֔ם מֶ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתָ לִ֑י לָקֹ֤ב אֹיְבַי֙ לְקַחְתִּ֔יךָ וְהִנֵּ֖ה בֵּרַ֥כְתָּ בָרֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: But Balaam replied, “Should I not speak exactly what the LORD puts in my mouth?”
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
Balak asked Balaam to curse Israel.
Balaam answered Balak.
Balaam said, “I must speak only what the LORD tells me.
I will say exactly what the LORD puts in my mouth.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֖עַן וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הֲלֹ֗א אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָשִׂ֤ים יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֔י אֹת֥וֹ אֶשְׁמֹ֖ר לְדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: Then Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place where you can see them. You will only see the outskirts of their camp—not all of them. And from there, curse them for me.”
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak spoke to Balaam.
Balak said, "Come with me to another place."
Balak wanted Balaam to see the people of Israel from a different location.
Balak said, "You will see only the edge of their camp."
Balak said, "You will not see all of the people."
Balak said, "Curse them for me from there."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו בָּלָ֗ק לְךָ נָּ֨א אִתִּ֜י אֶל־ מָק֤וֹם אַחֵר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּרְאֶ֣נּוּ מִשָּׁ֔ם אֶ֚פֶס קָצֵ֣הוּ תִרְאֶ֔ה וְכֻלּ֖וֹ לֹ֣א תִרְאֶ֑ה וְקָבְנוֹ־ לִ֖י מִשָּֽׁם׃

passages.text: So Balak took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, where he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak took Balaam with him.
They went to the field of Zophim.
This field was on the top of Pisgah.
Balak built seven altars there.
He offered a bull on each altar.
He also offered a ram on each altar.
passages.original: וַיִּקָּחֵ֙הוּ֙ שְׂדֵ֣ה צֹפִ֔ים אֶל־ רֹ֖אשׁ הַפִּסְגָּ֑ה וַיִּ֙בֶן֙ שִׁבְעָ֣ה מִזְבְּחֹ֔ת וַיַּ֛עַל פָּ֥ר וָאַ֖יִל בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: Balaam said to Balak, “Stay here beside your burnt offering while I meet the LORD over there.”
passages.sermon: Balaam spoke to Balak.\r\nBalaam told Balak to stand by his burnt offering.\r\nBalaam said he would go to meet the LORD.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ בָּלָ֔ק הִתְיַצֵּ֥ב כֹּ֖ה עַל־ עֹלָתֶ֑ךָ וְאָנֹכִ֖י אִקָּ֥רֶה כֹּֽה׃

passages.text: And the LORD met with Balaam and put a message in his mouth, saying, “Return to Balak and speak what I tell you.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD met with Balaam.
The LORD put a message in Balaam’s mouth.
The LORD said, “Return to Balak.”
The LORD said, “Speak what I tell you.”
passages.original: וַיִּקָּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיָּ֥שֶׂם דָּבָ֖ר בְּפִ֑יו וַיֹּ֛אמֶר שׁ֥וּב אֶל־ בָּלָ֖ק וְכֹ֥ה תְדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: So he returned to Balak, who was standing there by his burnt offering with the princes of Moab. “What did the LORD say?” Balak asked.
passages.sermon:
Balaam returned to Balak.
Balak was standing beside his burnt offering.
The princes of Moab stood with Balak.
Balak spoke to Balaam.
Balak asked, “What did the LORD say?”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵלָ֗יו וְהִנּ֤וֹ נִצָּב֙ עַל־ עֹ֣לָת֔וֹ וְשָׂרֵ֥י מוֹאָ֖ב אִתּ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ בָּלָ֔ק מַה־ דִּבֶּ֖ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Arise, O Balak, and listen; give ear to me, O son of Zippor.
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
God gave Balaam a message.
Balaam spoke the message as an oracle.
Balaam said, “Balak, stand up.
Listen to me.
Pay attention, son of Zippor.”
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר ק֤וּם בָּלָק֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔ע הַאֲזִ֥ינָה עָדַ֖י בְּנ֥וֹ צִפֹּֽר׃

passages.text: God is not a man, that He should lie, or a son of man, that He should change His mind. Does He speak and not act? Does He promise and not fulfill?
passages.sermon:
God is not a man.
God does not lie.
God is not a human being.
God does not change His mind.
When God says something, He does it.
When God speaks, He keeps His word.
When God makes a promise, He fulfills it.
passages.original: לֹ֣א אִ֥ישׁ אֵל֙ וִֽיכַזֵּ֔ב וּבֶן־ אָדָ֖ם וְיִתְנֶחָ֑ם הַה֤וּא אָמַר֙ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְדִבֶּ֖ר וְלֹ֥א יְקִימֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: I have indeed received a command to bless; He has blessed, and I cannot change it.
passages.sermon:
Balaam is a prophet.
God gave Balaam a command to bless Israel.
God has already blessed Israel.
I cannot change God’s blessing.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֥ה בָרֵ֖ךְ לָקָ֑חְתִּי וּבֵרֵ֖ךְ וְלֹ֥א אֲשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: He considers no disaster for Jacob; He sees no trouble for Israel. The LORD their God is with them, and the shout of the King is among them.
passages.sermon:
God is with the people of Israel.
God is with Jacob.
God does not see disaster in Jacob.
God does not see trouble in Israel.
The LORD is their God.
The shout of the King is among them.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ הִבִּ֥יט אָ֙וֶן֙ בְּיַעֲקֹ֔ב וְלֹא־ רָאָ֥ה עָמָ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וּתְרוּעַ֥ת מֶ֖לֶךְ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: God brought them out of Egypt with strength like a wild ox.
passages.sermon: God is the one who brought Israel out of Egypt.\r\nGod used great strength to do this.\r\nGod’s strength was like the strength of a wild ox.
passages.original: אֵ֖ל מוֹצִיאָ֣ם מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם כְּתוֹעֲפֹ֥ת רְאֵ֖ם לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For there is no spell against Jacob and no divination against Israel. It will now be said of Jacob and Israel, ‘What great things God has done!’
passages.sermon:
Jacob is the ancestor of the people of Israel.
Israel is the nation descended from Jacob.
No spell can harm Jacob.
No divination can harm Israel.
People will speak about Jacob and Israel.
They will say, “See what God has done!”
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹא־ נַ֙חַשׁ֙ בְּיַעֲקֹ֔ב וְלֹא־ קֶ֖סֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כָּעֵ֗ת יֵאָמֵ֤ר לְיַעֲקֹב֙ וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מַה־ פָּ֖עַל אֵֽל׃

passages.text: Behold, the people rise like a lioness; they rouse themselves like a lion, not resting until they devour their prey and drink the blood of the slain.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel are strong and bold.
They rise up like a lioness.
They stand tall like a lion.
They do not rest.
They do not lie down.
They keep going until they eat their prey.
They drink the blood of those they defeat.
passages.original: הֶן־ עָם֙ כְּלָבִ֣יא יָק֔וּם וְכַאֲרִ֖י יִתְנַשָּׂ֑א לֹ֤א יִשְׁכַּב֙ עַד־ יֹ֣אכַל טֶ֔רֶף וְדַם־ חֲלָלִ֖ים יִשְׁתֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Now Balak said to Balaam, “Then neither curse them at all nor bless them at all!”
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balaam was a prophet.
Balak spoke to Balaam.
Balak said, “Do not curse these people.
Do not bless them either.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בָּלָק֙ אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֔ם גַּם־ קֹ֖ב לֹ֣א תִקֳּבֶ֑נּוּ גַּם־ בָּרֵ֖ךְ לֹ֥א תְבָרֲכֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: But Balaam replied, “Did I not tell you that whatever the LORD says, I must do?”
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak wanted Balaam to curse Israel.
Balaam answered Balak.
Balaam said, “I told you this before.”
Balaam said, “I must do everything the LORD says.”
Balaam said, “I cannot do anything else.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַן בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֶל־ בָּלָ֑ק הֲלֹ֗א דִּבַּ֤רְתִּי אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ יְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֹת֥וֹ אֶֽעֱשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: “Please come,” said Balak, “I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God that you curse them for me from there.”
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak spoke to Balaam.
Balak said, "Please come with me."
Balak said, "I will take you to another place."
Balak said, "Perhaps God will be pleased there."
Balak said, "Maybe you can curse them for me from that place."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בָּלָק֙ אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֔ם לְכָה־ נָּא֙ אֶקָּ֣חֲךָ֔ אֶל־ מָק֖וֹם אַחֵ֑ר אוּלַ֤י יִישַׁר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְקַבֹּ֥תוֹ לִ֖י מִשָּֽׁם׃

passages.text: And Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the wasteland.
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balaam was a prophet.
Balak took Balaam with him.
They went to the top of Peor.
Peor is a mountain.
Peor overlooks the wasteland.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֥ח בָּלָ֖ק אֶת־ בִּלְעָ֑ם רֹ֣אשׁ הַפְּע֔וֹר הַנִּשְׁקָ֖ף עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הַיְשִׁימֹֽן׃

passages.text: Then Balaam said, “Build for me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet from outside Israel.
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak wanted Balaam to curse Israel.
Balaam spoke to Balak.
Balaam said, “Build seven altars for me here.”
Balaam said, “Prepare seven bulls for me here.”
Balaam said, “Prepare seven rams for me here.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בִּלְעָם֙ אֶל־ בָּלָ֔ק בְּנֵה־ לִ֥י בָזֶ֖ה שִׁבְעָ֣ה מִזְבְּחֹ֑ת וְהָכֵ֥ן לִי֙ בָּזֶ֔ה שִׁבְעָ֥ה פָרִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה אֵילִֽים׃

passages.text: So Balak did as Balaam had instructed, and he offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balaam was a prophet.
Balaam gave instructions to Balak.
Balak obeyed Balaam.
Balak built the altars as Balaam said.
Balak offered a bull on each altar.
Balak offered a ram on each altar.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ בָּלָ֔ק כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֣ר בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיַּ֛עַל פָּ֥ר וָאַ֖יִל בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
